title: Selecting an Assistant
text: We’re loading up on food in the Lazy Pig’s territory. The bio-plant fields are gradually expanding, and bio-plant cultivation is already well underway on a considerable scale in the Lazy Pig’s territory.

Some people even come from far away to buy food, and according to Father, business is booming. Part of the distribution is outsourced, and to a certain extent, the nation’s hunger has truly been alleviated—we’ve settled into a state where we no longer struggle to find food. I hear the Lazy Pig’s family home, which played a part in this, made a substantial profit. What an infuriating fact.

But if planting them recklessly just means someone else gets the credit, maybe it’s best to give up at some point. With that in mind, I’m loading food onto the wagon again today. Father says food has been selling better than medicine lately.
“Oink.”
Amidst all this, the Lazy Pig emerged from her family home and called out to my Father.
“Hm? What’s the matter, Elena?”
“Oink…”
“Eh…”
“Oink.”
For some reason, my Father seemed stunned by the Lazy Pig’s words; he let out a sigh of exasperation, yet at the same time, his expression turned tense.
“…Go get Wyndia.”
“Has something happened?”
“Yeah, I’ll talk to Motoyasu-kun too, so come with me.”
Father summoned everyone, including his assistant.
“What’s going on?”
Father approached his assistant and spoke.
“It seems a plague is spreading in the eastern village.”
At those words, the assistant, Keel, Yuki-chan, and the others all looked stunned.
“The cause is probably…”
Hesitating, my Father turned his gaze toward the Assistant and the monster. There’s no way they couldn’t tell what he was trying to say.

The Assistant stood quietly with his head bowed. As for the monster, it sat there demurely with its eyes closed. Nine times out of ten, there’s no doubt that the dragon’s carcass is the cause. After all, Father had repeatedly warned the villagers that it was dangerous and that they should dispose of it as soon as possible.

Filolial-sama, who has a keen sense of smell, and Keel had already said their noses were turning at the sight of the dragon’s carcass. There were plenty of warning signs at that point. Yet, to have ignored Father’s warnings—it’s truly a case of reaping what they sowed. They are utterly unworthy of being saved. It is a bit of a bummer that the plague was caused by the dragon, though.
“Wyndia-chan.”
My father grabs her by the shoulder, bringing himself to the Assistant’s eye level.
“You… what do you want me to do?”
“…Why are you asking me?”
“Because you’re involved.”
“I warned you plenty, and honestly, I’m under no obligation to help. Elena told me about this because she smelled money…”
The assistant looks down, averting her gaze.
“So I want to ask you this: Are you going to abandon them like this and watch as your father indirectly takes revenge on those villagers, or…”
After a brief pause, Father fixed the assistant with a piercing gaze and asked.
“Are you going to go save the village?”
Silence reigned over the area. Filolial-sama and the others stood there, each with a complex expression on their face.
“Big brother… Wyndia-chan.”
Keel looked back and forth between Father and the Assistant with a worried expression.
“Gau.”
The monster… gently nibbled at the hem of the Assistant’s clothes. The Assistant quietly placed a hand on the monster’s head and stroked it.

“We have no obligation to them, and they’re all terrible people. We could just abandon them. If our true identities were exposed, that would be a dangerous move—it might actually give them a justifiable reason to act. This situation is already turning into a full-blown incident, and maybe Itsuki, the Bow Hero, will be the one to resolve it.”
“I think abandoning them is probably the right choice. But I want you, Wyndia, to decide what to do.”
“Gau…”
The assistant locked eyes with the monster and muttered something under her breath in the monster’s language. Then she looked up…
“Shield Hero, please… please ward off the plague in that village… the calamity your father left behind. I beg you.”
A faint stream of tears was flowing from her eyes. Father placed his hand on the assistant’s head and gently stroked it.
“Yeah, that’s amazing… I think you’ve made a choice I’m very proud of. It might sound arrogant, but on behalf of your father, I want to praise you. It’s not a choice I could ever make myself.”
Suddenly, the assistant buried her face in Father’s chest.
“You’ve grown up to be such a good girl. Now, let’s go build a grave for your father.”
“Yeah… yeah…”
Father held her in a gentle embrace.
“Well then, so as not to waste Wyndia-chan’s resolve, we’re going to hurry off to the eastern village right away. Elena, check the medicine.”
“Boo…”
“Keel, please get the preventive medicine and masks ready. Sakura, Yuki, Kou, and Luna, get ready so we can leave at any moment!”
“Got it, big bro! Things are about to get busy!”
“‘‘‘Roger that!’’’”
Everyone started getting ready to leave all at once.
“Just to be safe, make sure we secure some antidotes and powerful potions! Motoyasu, I’m counting on you for that, too.”
“Leave it to me!”

I’ll use my spear skills to craft the potions. It’s no big deal—I can easily make powerful potions using the materials currently in my spear. I could even make the top-tier Yggdrasil potion, if I had to. However, given the materials available, it’d probably be better to mass-produce a version a few ranks lower.
“Gau!”
“Yeah, let’s go!”

At the Assistant’s words, a monster approached and crouched down near him, lowering its hips and head so he could jump onto its back immediately. This is an event tied to a past grudge. I seem to recall hearing that even in the future, there was a village struck by a plague.

This is likely the event in question. I don’t think my father knew the Assistant at that point. While my knowledge of the future is of little use, I don’t think this is a situation we can’t handle. Well then! This is where things get serious.

We kept our load light and hurried to the eastern village. Compared to last time, a strangely grim atmosphere hangs in the air even before we reach the eastern village. I don’t think it’s just my imagination that the temperature feels a bit lower.

Dark clouds hang over the mountains, the grasslands are black… I’m actually taken aback by these eerie changes myself. Not a single ray of sunlight breaks through the sky… an eerie atmosphere, like a scene from a horror movie I once went to see with Pig, dominates the surroundings. It seems the Filolial-sama feel the same way, as they all have stern, tense expressions on their faces.
“It’s changed quite a bit since the last time we were here. And it’s only been about two weeks.”
“Indeed.”
It was already clear from our first visit that the ecosystem had undergone major changes due to the defeat of that giant dragon. I suppose the miasma from the corpses has only added to that.
“I guess this is what you’d call the reality of another world…? Hmm, it feels downright ominous, doesn’t it?”
“If you think of it as being similar to a forest fire, isn’t that about right?”
“That might be true. Maybe the pollution of the earth is erupting in a visible form.”
“It stinks!”
“It’s enough to make my nose curl, bro.”
“Everyone took their preventive medicine so they don’t catch it, right?”
“Yeah.”
“Hmm…”
“Y-yes!”
Everyone nods. Of course, I took mine too. I made sure to give it to the Filolial-samas and watched them swallow it. That’s so they don’t secretly throw it away because it’s bitter.
“Gaelion, be especially careful—since this plague spread from your father, you might be the most susceptible.”
“Gau!”
The monster nodded at Father’s warning. My assistant has been staring intently at the mountains from the carriage the whole time.
“First, let’s check how much damage has been done in the village.”
“…Okay.”
“Also, Wyndia, try not to get out of the carriage—we don’t know what kind of trouble they might pick a fight over.”
“But…”
“It’s okay. I’ll definitely take you to where your father is.”
“…I understand.”
The assistant gripped the sleeve of her shirt tightly and nodded.
